my sleep has been terrible this week

Still worth pinning as a stemming case because 'morning' is a defensible signal and this measures the net hit.

value.evidence_quote: my sister Sarah visited this weekend
my weekend was busy with family
I saw an old friend last weekend

notes: Proper noun direct match. Token-recall should be the strong scorer here — 'sarah' is a high-signal token that appears only in f-sarah. Pure embedding might dilute the name across the sentence context and rank f-weekend or f-friend highly. This is the main 'why we chose hybrid over pure embedding' test case.

value.evidence_quote: I take fluoxetine daily for depression
I take vyvanse for ADHD
therapy has been helping with mood

query: did I say anything about fluoxetine
notes: Verbatim medication name. Token-recall is ideal here — 'fluoxetine' is a unique token. Pure embedding treats drug names as arbitrary strings and may cluster all three 'medication' facts together without strong separation. Hybrid RRF should recover via the token-recall contribution.

value.evidence_quote: I feel stuck and like nothing is moving forward

notes: Semantic paraphrase with zero token overlap: 'stuck', 'moving forward' (haystack) vs 'hopeless', 'right now' (query). Pure token-recall misses completely; embedding should catch via emotional-tone similarity. This is one of the 'you can't dogfood around' cases that justifies the whole embedding upgrade.

Note: f-meeting-anx is a near-miss — it mentions meetings (tangentially related) but is about anxiety, not attention. The eval should show pure-embedding and hybrid pulling f-focus, not f-meeting-anx.

value.evidence_quote: my sister Sarah visited this weekend
work has been really demanding
my sleep has been poor

notes: Single-word query. Token-recall wins cleanly (perfect recall on 'sarah'). Pure embedding on single-word queries is known to be weak — the embedding has little context to work with. This is a 'hybrid should stay as good as token-recall on proper-noun direct queries' test.

value.evidence_quote: work has been really demanding

notes: Four meaningful query tokens (things, tense, sarah, lately) but only 'sarah' has topical signal against the haystack. Recall = 1/4 = 0.25, which is BELOW the 0.33 token-recall threshold — so token-recall is EXPECTED TO MISS. This is the canonical low-signal failure mode that the embedding path should fix. The test pins it explicitly.
